dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Huh, this one is for the books. A lot of people avoid chatting with me whenever they can help it, because they don't like what I have to say.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The truth is, I just prefer it when people can cut to the chase and be straight with one another. The amount of effort some people put into beating around the bush and being diplomatic... It'd be so much quicker to just hash it out and be done with it.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: What about you? What's your preferred communication style?

choices.text: Direct and to the point, like you.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Excellent. That'll save us a lot of trouble.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I remember one time when I saw a customer hesitating between two different colored outfits.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I told her that she should pick the cream-colored one, since it went well with her hair and also accentuated her figure. She turned her nose up at that, and said that stains would show up more on the cream one than the gray one.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: So I said sure thing — if you're set on the gray one, I can make some adjustments so it'll look more stylish. But she didn't like that idea either, and she started saying that maybe the gray was a bit too dull.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We went back and forth like that for a whole afternoon. In the end? She picked a red one...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I mean, I do understand where she was coming from. Her concerns were valid, it's just... People like that... they need to learn to prioritize between criteria when they're making a decision.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: If you want something that goes with your figure, pick the cream. If you want to get away with a few smudges and stains, pick the gray.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: But if what you really want is to stand out from the crowd so your crush will spot you as soon as they arrive at the party... then for goodness' sake, just tell me that as soon as you walk through my door!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Phew... I'm getting all worked up just thinking about it. I need a moment to calm down...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You're right. She was hesitant about telling me. But if she'd just been direct with me, we could have saved so much time, and then I would have been able to do a better job of tailoring her outfit to suit her needs.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Things like that happen all the time. It makes me all the more determined to never beat around the bush, and always be upfront and direct.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Sure, it might not have been the smartest approach. But for me at least, it's definitely the most efficient.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: All this is to say that I will never hide my true thoughts and feelings from you, and I'd like it if you could do the same for me.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Of course, if you ever find yourself compelled to say something like "Chioriya Boutique's outfits are hideous"... then I'd hope you at least follow it up with some sort of reasoned argument that I can consider.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You don't seem like the type of person who'd say something just to be provocative. Unless... I dunno, you secretly enjoy the feeling of being thrown out of my front door, or something.

choices.text: I think sometimes, being tactful is better than being blunt...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You do? Well, I just find it a headache.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Maybe it's because I always have a clear and firm opinion on things. My feelings are never ambiguous — either I like something, or I don't.
